evidence.title: Monstera
evidence.text: Monstera is a genus of about 50 species of flowering plants in the arum family, Araceae, native to tropical regions of the Americas.

evidence.title: Monstera
evidence.text: The genus is named from the Latin word for "monstrous" or "abnormal", and refers to the unusual leaves with natural holes that members of the genus have.

evidence.title: Rhaphidophora tetrasperma
evidence.text: Rhaphidophora tetrasperma (common names: "Mini Monstera", Philodendron "Ginny", Philodendron "Piccolo") is a species of plant in the family Araceae, genus "Rhaphidophora".

evidence.title: Rhaphidophora tetrasperma
evidence.text: It is native to Southern Thailand and to Malaysia.

evidence.title: Cercis
evidence.text: Cercis , is a genus of about 10 species in the subfamily Cercidoideae of the pea family Fabaceae, native to warm temperate regions.

evidence.title: Cercis
evidence.text: It contains small deciduous trees or large shrubs commonly known as redbuds.

evidence.title: Cercis
evidence.text: They are characterised by simple, rounded to heart-shaped leaves and pinkish-red flowers borne in the early spring on bare leafless shoots, on both branches and trunk ("cauliflory").

evidence.title: Cercis
evidence.text: Cercis is derived from the Greek word κερκις ("kerkis") meaning "weaver's shuttle", which was applied by Theophrastus to "C. siliquastrum".

evidence.title: Cercidiphyllum
evidence.text: Cercidiphyllum is a genus containing two species of plants, both commonly called katsura.

evidence.title: Cercidiphyllum
evidence.text: They are the sole members of the monotypic family Cercidiphyllaceae.

evidence.title: Cercidiphyllum
evidence.text: The genus is native to Japan and China and unrelated to "Cercis" (redbuds).
